# Modal

Figma: [06d. Modal](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-934) · Family: 06 Navigation · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-06-14

A centered overlay for a focused task that interrupts the flow until resolved. The desktop-and-tablet twin of BottomSheet - same SheetHeader, SheetFooter, and content library, in a centered card with sm · md · lg · xl widths, across LTR + RTL.

### Modal

Centered overlay card on a dimmed scrim that blocks the page until the user acts; the web/desktop twin of BottomSheet sharing SheetHeader, SheetFooter and the content library, in four widths. Reserved for critical interruptions.

Level: organism · Contains: SheetHeader, SheetFooter, Sheet Content / Blank, Sheet Content / Media

Use when:
- Critical or irreversible actions on web (delete, discard changes)
- Information the flow cannot continue without (sign in to save a deal)
- Media-rich explainer video or gallery on web (Size=xl with Sheet Content / Media)
- Back-office forms or summaries that need focus (Size=md/lg)

Don't use when:
- On mobile: use BottomSheet
- Simple one-line yes/no confirm: use Dialog
- Promos, announcements or upsells during checkout: do not interrupt; use Banner or inline content
- Side panels for filters or detail: use Drawer

Accessibility: role=dialog aria-modal, focus trapped and returned to the trigger, Esc closes routine modals; for destructive confirms disable scrim/Esc dismissal and require an explicit choice.

| Property in Figma | Code name | Type | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| showHeader | `showHeader` | boolean |  | true |
| showFooter | `showFooter` | boolean |  | true |
| Content | `content` | instance swap | default Sheet Content / Blank | 2699:12 |
| Size | `size` | variant | sm, md, lg, xl | sm |
| Direction | `direction` | variant | LTR, RTL | LTR |

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

A Modal is a centered overlay that puts the screen into a special mode: it dims and disables everything behind it and demands an action before the user can continue. That power is also its cost - it interrupts the task, hides context, and adds a step (dismiss it). Reserve it for moments that genuinely deserve the interruption.

### When to use

- Critical, irreversible actions - warn before data loss or a destructive step (delete, discard unsaved changes).
- Information required to continue - the system can’t proceed without it (sign in to favourite a deal).
- Breaking one complex action into a short wizard - with clear progress; if it needs many steps, use a full page.
- A single, low-effort question that streamlines the task (progressive profiling - ask one relevant thing).

### When not to use

- Nonessential or unrelated prompts - newsletter sign-ups, promos, announcements. These erode trust fast.
- During high-stakes flows like checkout - never interrupt a purchase to upsell or ask to log in.
- Decisions that need information the modal hides - if the user must go research, don’t trap them.
- On mobile - prefer BottomSheet (06c); for a one-line confirm, prefer Dialog (05h).

> **Warning:** No one likes to be interrupted - if you must, make sure it’s worth the cost. For non-critical tasks, prefer a nonmodal surface (inline panel, toast, or a side sheet) that lets people keep working.

### Live preview

### Anatomy

A centered card floating on a dimmed scrim - the same five-part stack as BottomSheet, minus the drag handle.

- Scrim - dimmed overlay (bg/overlay) covering the screen; clicking it dismisses.
- Card - centered container, all corners Radius/24, bg/base, with a drop shadow to lift it off the scrim.
- Header (SheetHeader) - title, optional subtitle, close; toggle with showHeader.
- Content slot - the swappable body; fills the card width.
- Footer (SheetFooter) - primary + optional secondary action; toggle with showFooter.

> **Info:** Modal shares the SheetHeader and SheetFooter atoms and the entire content library with BottomSheet - edit an atom once and both surfaces update.

### Sizes

Four width tiers; height always hugs content. Pick the smallest that fits. On web, modals can be large - the xl tier is built for media-rich content like an explainer video or gallery.

- sm - 400px · compact confirmations and short messages.
- md - 520px · the default; standard content, forms, summaries.
- lg - 680px · richer content - lists, detailed breakdowns.
- xl - 880px · media-rich modals (video, image gallery). Don’t stretch plain paragraphs this wide - keep text columns readable.

### Content library

Modal shares BottomSheet’s content library and adds Media for the xl tier. Swap any of these - or your own component - into the Content slot.

Text

Heading, paragraphs, and a link.

List

Selectable rows with a Tag chip.

Summary

KeyValue rows with an emphasized total.

Amount

Input Amount with a Slider.

Form

Input and TextArea fields.

Empty state

The EmptyState component.

Media

A 16:9 video/image block with caption - pairs with the xl size.

Blank / Custom

An empty slot. Swap it in, then drop your own component - or detach to edit freely. The Modal’s default content.

### Composition & slots

Same composable model as BottomSheet: toggle the chrome, swap the content.

### Chrome toggles

- showHeader - show or hide the SheetHeader (which toggles showSubtitle and showClose).
- showFooter - show or hide the SheetFooter (showSecondary for one- vs two-button stacks).

### Content slot

- Set the Content property to swap the body - 7 presets including Media for the xl size.
- Swap in any component; the default is a placeholder meant to be replaced.

> **Info:** For a destructive confirm, hide the close (showClose=false) and keep both footer actions so the choice is explicit; for routine modals, keep an easy way out.

### Direction - LTR and RTL

The Direction axis flips the chrome; the content carries its own Direction.

LTR

Left-to-right, IBM Plex Sans. Close on the trailing (right) side.

RTL

Right-to-left, Noto Sans Arabic. Header mirrors; content right-aligns.

- Set the Modal Direction to flip header and footer; match the Content instance’s own Direction.

### Behavior & dismissal

A modal takes over the screen - entering a mode - so appearance and exit must be deliberate.

- Scrim - dims and disables the background; the page beneath cannot be interacted with until the modal resolves.
- Dismissal - click the scrim, the close, or Esc for routine modals. There is no drag-to-dismiss (that is a BottomSheet affordance).
- One at a time - never stack modals. Competing overlays (overlay overload) frustrate users and bury the real task.
- Focus - trap focus inside while open; restore it to the trigger on close.
- Height - the card hugs content; long content scrolls inside while header and footer stay pinned.

> **Warning:** For critical or destructive confirmations, disable scrim-click and Esc dismissal and require an explicit choice - so the user can’t lose work by clicking away. For everything else, make leaving effortless.

### Code examples

### Flutter

```dart
showDialog(
  context: context,
  barrierColor: SyntropyColors.bgOverlay,
  barrierDismissible: !isCritical,   // block dismiss for destructive confirms
  builder: (context) => SyntropyModal(
    size: ModalSize.md,              // sm · md · lg · xl
    header: SheetHeader(
      title: 'Discard changes?',
      subtitle: 'Your edits will be lost.',
      showClose: !isCritical,
    ),
    content: const TextContent(),    // swap any content (Media for xl)
    footer: SheetFooter(
      primary: Button.primary('Discard', onPressed: _discard),
      secondary: Button.secondary('Keep editing', onPressed: () => Navigator.pop(context)),
    ),
  ),
);
```

### Usage - Do and Don’t

Do

Do interrupt to confirm a critical or irreversible action - review the impact, then confirm.

Don’t

Don’t interrupt with nonessential promos or newsletter sign-ups - it erodes trust and gets ignored.

Do

Do use a modal to collect information the flow genuinely can’t continue without (e.g. sign in to subscribe).

Don’t

Don’t interrupt high-stakes flows like checkout to upsell or ask to log in - let people finish.

### Notes from the maintainer

> **Info:** Modal is the centered twin of BottomSheet: it reuses the SheetHeader, SheetFooter, and the entire content library. Editing those atoms updates both surfaces.

> **Info:** Web modals run large - the xl (880) size plus the Media content cover video and image-gallery modals. Keep plain text columns narrower (sm/md) for readability.

> **Warning:** The Content slot has one shared default across all 8 variants (a Figma limit) - it defaults to the English Text placeholder; for RTL, swap to the RTL content variant.

> **Warning:** Reserve modals for critical interruptions (NN/g): irreversible actions, required input, focused wizard steps. For anything non-critical, prefer a nonmodal surface so people keep working.

> **Warning:** The card drop shadow is a raw rgba effect - add effect/shadow/* tokens later.
